increments.title: Content-bearing telemetry is captured by default and served over the API
increments.goal: Turn the content flags on by default in `argus env` and make the collector store and serve what the resulting events carry, so a caller can ask for the conversation content belonging to a point in time.
criteria: `argus env` includes the content flags by default in both output formats: user prompts, tool details, tool content, and the flag or flags the CLI requires to emit `api_request_body`/`api_response_body` events.
The exact flag names are verified against the CLI's monitoring documentation rather than assumed.
If the current CLI turns out not to emit request/response body events at all, that is reported as an explicit finding, naming the best content the available flags do provide.
What attribution actually arrives for subagent activity and for request bodies is established and reported, including any gap, so later increments know which records can be assigned to which agent.

The collector stores the content those events carry and exposes those content-bearing records over the JSON API like the existing signals, such that the content belonging to a point in time can be asked for.
Recordings made without the content flags are out of contract: no fallback rendering, no compatibility notice, and no test pins behavior for them.
`./test.sh` is green.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings: the four content flags (OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_DETAILS, OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT, OTEL_LOG_RAW_API_BODIES=1) are on by default in all four env formats, contentOf plus store.queryContent plus GET /api/content store and serve the content-bearing records with an inclusive 'at' bound, and the suite is green (156 argus cases exit 0; bash ./test.sh PASS all 6 suites). The attribution gap is established: body events carry query_source and span context but no agent.name or agent_id.

increments.title: A session opens on the timeline, with a lane per agent
increments.goal: Make opening a session in the argus UI land on a timeline view that draws one lane for the main session and one per subagent across each agent's lifetime, with the existing technical views reachable from it but subordinate.
criteria: Opening a session in the argus UI lands on the timeline view.
The previous technical views — event tail, traces, raw inspectors — remain reachable from the timeline view and are subordinate to it, not the other way round.

The timeline draws one lane for the main session and one lane per subagent instance, so two concurrent subagents of the same type get two lanes; `query_source` names only the agent type, and per-instance identity has to come from the span attributes the previous increment reported (`agent_id`, `parent_agent_id`).
Each agent lane spans that agent's lifetime, so any vertical slice answers which agents are running at that moment.

Where the run places the record-to-agent join — collector side or UI side — that choice is stated, and activity that cannot be attributed to an agent instance is shown as unattributed rather than dropped or silently folded into the main session.
increments.note: Review accepted with no findings after two correction rounds, both of them test gaps rather than defects. What shipped: a collector-side lane join in store.getAgents behind GET /api/sessions/:id/agents, giving every span of a session a lane key of 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed' by resolving agent_id first and the parent-span chain second; a timeline module in argus-ui drawing one bar per lane over one shared window; and the six technical views (overview, todos, traces, events, metrics, raw) moved into a strip below the timeline, closed by default. npm --prefix tools/argus test 176 cases exit 0, npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test 39 cases exit 0. Both correction rounds were spent because the visible behaviour was computed by a tested pure helper but never pinned in the rendered markup or the booted page; the round-2 fake-DOM harness in tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs now boots public/app.js in-process, so later UI increments have a way to pin what the human sees.

increments.title: Activity and context growth drawn on each lane
increments.goal: Draw each lane's activity over time and, behind it, that agent's context size over time, so where token consumption grows is visible on the timeline itself.
criteria: Each lane shows its activity over time - tool calls and API requests - placed at the times they occurred, on the lane of the agent instance the activity belongs to.

Activity is assigned to lanes with the lane vocabulary the session's agents endpoint already serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed'), not a second attribution scheme; the records drawn here carry no agent_id of their own, so where their lane comes from is stated.
Activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane rather than being dropped or folded into the main lane.
Each lane carries, as a curve or area behind that activity, the context size over time for that agent.

The curve is drawn from a size the telemetry actually records - the reported untruncated request-body length survives even when the body itself was truncated - and the view names which measure it is showing.
Growth in context size is readable from the timeline alone, without opening any detail.
What proves this increment is the drawn result in the page: a change that stops the activity marks or the curve reaching the rendered timeline is caught, not only a computation checked in isolation.
increments.note: Re-cut after timeline-landing. Two criteria added and one sharpened. Timeline-landing established a lane vocabulary collector-side - every span of a session resolves to 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed', by agent_id first and the parent-span chain second, served by GET /api/sessions/:id/agents - so this increment inherits it instead of inventing per-lane attribution again, and the unattributed lane it already draws must keep receiving what cannot be attributed. Content-pipeline showed the body events carry no agent_id, so the same span-chain resolution is the only route from a record to a lane, and that route is the one open question its researcher settles first. The provability criterion is there because both correction rounds of timeline-landing were spent on exactly this: the geometry and the landing were computed correctly by tested pure helpers while nothing pinned that they reached the page.

return.summary: Extend the existing collector-side lane join (store.getAgents) so every lane carries its tool/llm_request activity marks and a context-size series read from api_request_body body_length, and draw both in timeline.js as per-lane ticks over an SVG area behind the lane bar, with the measure named in the panel.
return.plan: GOAL Each timeline lane gains two drawn things: marks for that agent's tool calls and API requests at the times they happened, and behind them an area whose height is that agent's context size over time. Nothing about lanes themselves changes. WHERE THE LANE OF EACH DRAWN RECORD COMES FROM (the load-bearing decision) The join stays collector-side and reuses the one function that already produces the 'main' / 'agent:' / 'unattributed' vocabulary: `laneKeyOf` inside `TelemetryStore#getAgents` (tools/argus/src/store.mjs, around line 860). No second attribution scheme is introduced and no new endpoint is added. - Activity marks come from spans named `claude_code.tool` and `claude_code.llm_request` (SPAN.tool, SPAN.llmRequest). They are already walked by the getAgents span loop, so each mark takes the very lane key that loop computed for its span — agent_id when the span carries one, otherwise the parent-span chain, otherwise main for a parentless span, otherwise unattributed. Do not emit marks for `claude_code.tool.execution` spans: they are children of the tool span and would double-count every call. - The context series comes from `claude_code.api_request_body` log events (EVENT.apiRequestBody). These records carry no `agent_id` at all — content-pipeline established that they carry only `query_source` and span context. Their lane is therefore resolved through their span: `log.spanId` is looked up in the same `byId` span map getAgents already builds, and the found span's lane key is used. A log with no `spanId`, or whose span is not in the buffer, lands on the unattributed lane — never on main, and never dropped. `query_source` is deliberately not used as a fallback: it names the agent type, not the instance, and using it would be exactly the second attribution scheme the increment forbids. WHAT THE CURVE IS MADE OF The sample value is `contentOf(log).length` from tools/argus/src/claude.mjs — the reported untruncated `body_length`, which survives when the CLI truncated the body (`body_truncated=1`, short `body`) and also when only a `body_ref` arrived. Never `text.length`. Only `request_body` kind feeds the curve; `api_response_body`, `user_prompt` and `tool_result` content are not context sent to the model and contribute nothing. Rejected alternative: `input_tokens` on `claude_code.api_request` events — arguably the truer token measure, but the criterion names the reported request-body length, and mixing two measures in one curve would need the view to name two things. COLLECTOR CHANGES — tools/argus/src/store.mjs, `getAgents(sessionId)` only 1. Lane factory gains four keys, always present so the UI needs no shape checks: `activity: []`, `activityTotal: 0`, `context: []`, `contextPeak: 0`. 2. Pull the get-or-create of a lane out of the span loop into a small helper (e.g. `laneFor(key)`) so the content pass can create the unattributed lane when only a content record needs it. A lane created that way has `spanCount: 0`. 3. In the span loop, when `span.name` is SPAN.tool or SPAN.llmRequest and `span.startMs > 0`, push `{ atMs: span.startMs, kind: 'tool' | 'llm_request', name: attrs.tool_name ?? attrs.model ?? null }` onto that lane's activity. No duration on a mark: the lane bar already shows lifetime and a tick is what is drawn. 4. After the span loop, walk `this.logs` once: skip records of other sessions and every `eventName` other than EVENT.apiRequestBody; call `contentOf(log)` and skip a null; resolve the lane as described above; push `{ atMs: log.timeMs, length: content.length }` onto that lane's context, skipping `timeMs <= 0`. 5. Extend lane bounds with the times of activity and context entries (same `startMs > 0` guard the span bounds use), so a mark or a sample can never sit outside the lifetime its lane claims, and an unattributed lane born from content records alone still has a real firstMs/lastMs. The payload-level firstMs/lastMs derive from the lanes, so they follow. 6. Sort each lane's activity and context ascending by `atMs` (log/span arrival order is not guaranteed to be time order), then set `activityTotal` / `contextPeak` from the full lists, then bound them: - `const MAX_LANE_ACTIVITY = 2000;` even-stride downsample — `stride = Math.ceil(list.length / max)`, keep every stride-th, append the last element if the stride missed it. Keeping the newest N instead is wrong here: it would silently cut the left half off a long lane. - `const MAX_LANE_CONTEXT = 1000;` bucket-maximum downsample — split into `ceil(n/max)`-sized buckets in order and keep the largest sample of each, so the peak of the curve survives being thinned and the drawn area still reaches `contextPeak`. Both bounds exist because `/api/sessions/:id/agents` is refetched on every coalesced ingest while a session is live. 7. Update the `getAgents` docstring: lanes are built from spans and from the content records that resolve to no span, and none are invented beyond that. No change to `/api/sessions/:id/agents` in server.mjs: it serialises whatever getAgents returns. UI CHANGES — tools/argus-ui/public/timeline.js All of it pure and exported, so it is pinnable without a DOM (the module still must not touch document/window/location). - `export const MIN_AREA_WIDTH_PCT = 0.4;` alongside the existing MIN_WIDTH_PCT. - `export function contextPeakOf(items = [])` — the largest `contextPeak` over all lanes, 0 when none. One session-wide scale so lanes are comparable at a glance. - `export function activityMarks(lane, window)` — for each entry of `lane.activity ?? []` with `atMs > 0`, `{ leftPct: clampPct(((atMs - startMs) / Math.max(endMs - startMs, 1)) * 100), kind, name }`. Marks outside the window clamp to 0 or 100 rather than being dropped. - `export function contextAreaPoints(lane, window, peak)` — returns '' when the lane has no usable samples or `peak <= 0`. Otherwise map each sample to `{ x: clampPct(((atMs - startMs) / total) * 100), y: clampPct(100 - (length / peak) * 100) }`; if `lastX - firstX < MIN_AREA_WIDTH_PCT`, append one more point at `{ x: Math.min(100, firstX + MIN_AREA_WIDTH_PCT), y: lastY }` so a single-sample lane is still visible; then return the string `",100.000 , … , ,100.000"` with every number `toFixed(3)` and pairs joined by single spaces. Coordinates are viewBox units, which is why the SVG is `viewBox="0 0 100 100" preserveAspectRatio="none"`: percentages map straight through with no measurement of the DOM. - `timelineHtml(items, window)` computes `const peak = contextPeakOf(items)` once and, inside each `.lane-track`, renders in this order so the curve sits behind: first `` (omitted entirely when the points string is empty), then the existing `.lane-bar`, then one `` per mark, `left` formatted `toFixed(3)` like the bar and the title escaped with `esc`. - The lane label gains, after the spans count: `${fmtNum(lane.activityTotal)} calls` when `activityTotal > 0`, and `${fmtNum(lane.contextPeak)}` when `contextPeak > 0`, so per-lane growth is readable as a number as well as a shape. - Below the lane rows, inside the panel, a legend paragraph that names the measure. With a peak it must contain the phrase "request body length", the word "characters" and the session peak (e.g. "Curve: context size as the reported API request body length in characters, scaled to the session peak of 90.0k · marks: tool calls and API requests"). With no peak anywhere it must still contain "request bod" and say that none were recorded; no polygon is drawn in that case. - Every read of `lane.activity`, `lane.activityTotal`, `lane.context`, `lane.contextPeak` defaults (`?? []`, `?? 0`), so a lane payload without them renders exactly today's row. CSS — tools/argus-ui/public/styles.css, the timeline block near line 786 Give the curve room and keep the stack readable: `.lane-track` height from 18px to about 26px; `.lane-bar` becomes a thin lifetime strip at the top (e.g. `top: 2px; height: 4px`); `.lane-context { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100% }` with a translucent fill on its polygon; `.activity-mark { position: absolute; top: 8px; bottom: 2px; width: 2px; margin-left: -1px }` with distinct colours per `data-activity-kind`; small muted styles for `.lane-activity-count`, `.lane-context-peak` and `.timeline-legend`. Pixels are the implementer's; no test asserts them. DEMO — tools/argus/scripts/demo-emit.mjs Without this the curve cannot be looked at locally at all, since no synthetic session emits a body event today. Hoist the `spanId` of the main-turn `llm_request` span in `emitLlmCall` and of the subagent `llm_request` span into variables, extend the local `record(...)` helper with an optional span id (default stays `interactionId`, existing call sites unchanged), and emit one `claude_code.api_request_body` per llm span carrying that span id, a short `body`, and a `body_length` that grows with the turn sequence and the call index (plus jitter), so `npm --prefix tools/argus run demo` produces a rising curve on the main lane and on the subagent lanes. Nothing tests scripts/ today and nothing is added to test it. WHAT IS NOT TOUCHED `tools/argus-ui/public/app.js` and `index.html` need no change: app.js already hands the whole `/agents` payload to `timelineHtml`, so the new fields flow through untouched — that is what the booted-page test proves. `tools/argus-ui` must keep importing nothing from `tools/argus` (test/independence.test.mjs). Scrubbing, a chosen time, live mode and any per-lane detail panel belong to later increments and must not appear here. REJECTED ALTERNATIVES - A second endpoint (`/api/sessions/:id/activity`): it would repeat the lane join, add a second fetch, and let lanes and activity disagree after an eviction. - Doing the join in the browser from `/api/events` plus `/api/content`: the UI would have to rebuild the parent-span chain the collector already walks, which is the second attribution scheme the criteria forbid. - Drawing activity from `claude_code.api_request` / `claude_code.tool_result` log events instead of spans: those carry no agent_id either and would need the same span join for no gain, and without spans there are no lanes to draw them on anyway. - Per-lane y scaling of the curve: it makes every lane look equally full and hides which agent actually consumes the context.
return.moduleMap:
tools/argus/src/store.mjs — the in-memory store; `getAgents(sessionId)` (line ~846) is the only function that changes: its lane factory gains activity/activityTotal/context/contextPeak, its span loop emits activity marks, and a new pass over `this.logs` adds the context samples. Two module-level constants (MAX_LANE_ACTIVITY, MAX_LANE_CONTEXT) and two small downsample helpers join the ones already at the top.
tools/argus/src/claude.mjs — unchanged; supplies `EVENT.apiRequestBody`, `SPAN.tool`, `SPAN.llmRequest` and `contentOf(log)`, whose `length` is the reported untruncated body length (already imported by store.mjs).
tools/argus/src/server.mjs — unchanged; `GET /api/sessions/:id/agents` (line ~230) serialises whatever getAgents returns.
tools/argus/scripts/demo-emit.mjs — synthetic session emitter; `record(...)` gains an optional span id and `emitLlmCall` plus the subagent block emit `claude_code.api_request_body` logs with growing `body_length`.
tools/argus-ui/public/timeline.js — the pure timeline view model; gains MIN_AREA_WIDTH_PCT, `contextPeakOf`, `activityMarks`, `contextAreaPoints`, and a `timelineHtml` that renders the SVG area, the activity marks, the per-lane counts and the measure legend.
tools/argus-ui/public/styles.css — the timeline block from line 786: taller lane track, thinner lane bar, and styles for .lane-context, .activity-mark, .lane-activity-count, .lane-context-peak, .timeline-legend.
tools/argus-ui/public/app.js — unchanged; already passes the whole `/agents` payload into `timelineHtml(state.agents, state.agentWindow)` (line ~168, loaded in `loadAgents` line ~841).
tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs — collector cases for the lane join of activity and context.
tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs — one case over HTTP that the fields survive ingest and serialisation.
tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs — the drawn geometry and markup.
tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs — the booted page, proving marks and curve reach the rendered timeline.
return.environment:
Node v22.22.2 is installed; both packages are zero-dependency and declare Node >= 20.11, so no `npm install` is needed and none should be run.
Run the collector suite: `npm --prefix tools/argus test` (node --test over tools/argus/test/*.test.mjs).
Run the interface suite: `npm --prefix tools/argus-ui test` (node --test over tools/argus-ui/test/*.test.mjs).
Run one file while working: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`, `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs`.
Eyeball the result by hand (not part of the checks): `node tools/argus/bin/argus.mjs` in one shell, `node tools/argus/scripts/demo-emit.mjs` in a second, `node tools/argus-ui/bin/argus-ui.mjs` in a third, then open http://127.0.0.1:4319.
There is no linter, no formatter and no build step in this repository, and there is no root package.json.
return.testPlan:
Tests are needed. Four files, all `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, all cases added to files that already exist. I ran nothing: the two suites were last reported green (tools/argus 176 cases exit 0, tools/argus-ui 39 cases exit 0) at the end of the timeline-landing increment, and nothing has touched them since, so the only red at the start of this increment is the new cases below. Do not run a baseline.

===== A. tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs =====
Framework node:test. Conventions of this file: fixtures come from the module-level helpers `span(name, attributes, extra)` (times are offsets added to `NOW`, default spanId 'span-1'), `subagentSpan(name, agentId, extraAttrs, extra)` (sets agent_id/parent_agent_id/query_source) and `log(eventName, attributes, timeMs)` (session 'sess-1' via the SESSION constant, and note its `spanId` is '' — a case that needs a span id spreads it: `{ ...log('claude_code.api_request_body', {...}, t), spanId: 'llm' }`). Attribute values are written as strings, like the CLI sends them. Store is constructed per case with `new TelemetryStore()`, records go in with `store.ingest('traces'|'logs', [...])`, and assertions read `store.getAgents(SESSION)`. Test names are lowercase sentences describing the behaviour. Add a new section after the `getAgents: unattributed activity` block, headed `/* --------------- getAgents: activity and context per lane --------------- */`. Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/store.test.mjs`.

A1 — criterion: activity is placed on the lane of the agent instance it belongs to, at the time it occurred. Input: a main `claude_code.interaction` span (spanId 'root'), a subagent `claude_code.tool` span for agt-a (spanId 'tool-a', parent 'root', startMs 100, tool_name 'Read'), a subagent `claude_code.llm_request` span for agt-a (spanId 'llm-a', parent 'root', startMs 300, model 'claude-opus-5'). Expected: the 'agent:agt-a' lane's `activity` is `[{atMs: NOW+100, kind: 'tool', name: 'Read'}, {atMs: NOW+300, kind: 'llm_request', name: 'claude-opus-5'}]` in that order, `activityTotal` 2; the main lane's `activity` is `[]` (an interaction span is not activity). Level: unit.

A2 — criterion: activity that resolves to no agent instance stays on the unattributed lane. Input: interaction span 'root' plus a `claude_code.tool` span with `parentSpanId: 'ghost'` and no agent attributes. Expected: the unattributed lane's activity has that one mark, main's activity is empty. Level: unit.

A3 — criterion: the context curve is per lane, joined through the record's span because the record carries no agent_id. Input: interaction 'root'; subagent `claude_code.llm_request` for agt-a with spanId 'llm-a'; an `api_request_body` log at time NOW+50 with `{ body: '{"m":1}', body_length: '4096' }` and `spanId: 'llm-a'`. Expected: the 'agent:agt-a' lane's `context` is `[{atMs: NOW+50, length: 4096}]`, its `contextPeak` is 4096, and main's `context` is `[]`. Level: unit.

A4 — criterion (headline): the reported untruncated length survives truncation. Same shape as A3 but the log carries `{ body: '{"m":1}', body_truncated: 'true', body_length: '120000' }`. Expected: the sample's `length` is 120000 (not 7) and `contextPeak` is 120000. Level: unit.

A5 — criterion: a context record that resolves to no agent instance stays visible on the unattributed lane. Input: interaction 'root' plus an `api_request_body` log with `spanId: 'gone'` (no such span) at NOW+400, body_length '900'. Expected: an unattributed lane exists, its `context` holds that sample, main's `context` is empty, and the lane's `firstMs`/`lastMs` include NOW+400 (so its bar is drawable). Level: unit. Repeat once with `spanId: ''` (the fixture default) in the same case to cover "no span context at all".

A6 — criterion: only request bodies feed the curve. Input: interaction 'root', llm span 'llm-a' (main, parented to root), and three logs on spanId 'llm-a': `api_response_body` (body_length '5000'), `user_prompt` (prompt/prompt_length), `api_request_body` (body_length '1000'). Expected: the main lane's `context` has exactly one sample, length 1000, `contextPeak` 1000. Level: unit.

A7 — edge, empty: a lane with no tool/llm spans and no bodies still carries the four keys. Input: a session with only an interaction span. Expected: the main lane deep-equals `{activity: [], activityTotal: 0, context: [], contextPeak: 0}` on those four keys. Level: unit.

A8 — edge, limit: activity is bounded without losing the ends. Input: 3000 `claude_code.tool` spans on one subagent lane with startMs 1..3000 (build with a loop over `subagentSpan`, distinct spanIds, all parented to 'root'). Expected: `activityTotal` is 3000, `activity.length` is less than 3000, the first entry's atMs is NOW+1 and the last entry's atMs is NOW+3000. Level: unit.

A9 — edge, limit: the context peak survives thinning. Input: 1500 `api_request_body` logs on one span, lengths mostly 1000 but one 999999 in the middle. Expected: `contextPeak` is 999999, `context.length` is less than 1500, and `context.some(s => s.length === 999999)` is true. Level: unit.

Deliberately untested here: the exact downsampled length and the constants themselves (a bound, not a contract); eviction interaction (the existing eviction cases already cover the buffers these queries read).

===== B. tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs =====
Framework node:test over a real `createServer({ store })` on port 0 through the `withServer(options, run)` helper; payloads are built by `agentsTracePayload(sessionId)` (protobuf, via `encodeMessage(..., EXPORT_TRACE_REQUEST)`) and `contentLogsPayloadJson(sessionId, records)` (OTLP/JSON, records are `[{eventName, timeMs, attrs}]`). The convention in this file is to assert the ingest POST's status 200 first, so a failed POST reports as a failed POST. Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus/test/server.test.mjs`.

B1 — criterion: the drawn data actually reaches a client over HTTP, decoded from the wire. Extend `contentLogsPayloadJson` so a record may carry a `spanId` (emit `spanId: record.spanId` on the log record when present; hex, e.g. `'33'.repeat(8)`, which is the tool span id `agentsTracePayload` already uses for agt-a). New case, placed next to the two existing `/agents` cases: POST `agentsTracePayload('s-lane-activity')` to `/v1/traces` (assert 200), POST a `contentLogsPayloadJson('s-lane-activity', [...])` with one `claude_code.api_request_body` on spanId `'33'.repeat(8)` carrying `body`, `body_truncated: 'true'` and `body_length: '65000'` (assert 200), then GET `/api/sessions/s-lane-activity/agents`. Expected: status 200; the 'agent:agt-a' lane has one activity entry with `kind: 'tool'`, and one context entry whose `length` is 65000, with `contextPeak` 65000; every lane in the payload has the keys `activity`, `activityTotal`, `context`, `contextPeak`. Level: integration.

Deliberately untested here: the 404 for an unknown session and the lane shapes themselves (already pinned by the two existing cases).

===== C. tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs =====
Framework node:test, importing named exports from `../public/timeline.js`; no DOM anywhere in this file and none may be introduced. Conventions: the local `lane({id, kind, agentId, parentAgentId, agentType, firstMs, lastMs})` factory builds a payload item — extend it with optional `activity = []`, `activityTotal = activity.length`, `context = []`, `contextPeak` (max of the context lengths) so cases stay one line; windows are plain `{startMs: 0, endMs: 1000}` objects with small integers; markup assertions use a regex helper over the returned html (`laneBars(html)` is the existing example). Add a helper `laneRow(html, id)` that returns the substring of the markup from `data-lane-id="<id>"` to the next `data-lane-id="` (or the end), so a case can assert what is inside one row. Add a section headed `/* -------------------------- activity marks and the context curve -------------------------- */`. Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/timeline.test.mjs`.

C1 — criterion: activity is placed at the time it occurred. `activityMarks(lane with activity [{atMs: 250, kind:'tool'}, {atMs: 750, kind:'llm_request'}], {startMs: 0, endMs: 1000})` returns leftPct 25 and 75 with those kinds, in order. Level: unit.

C2 — edges of C1: an entry at atMs 0 or below is dropped; an entry before the window start clamps to 0 and one past the end clamps to 100 (window {startMs: 1000, endMs: 2000}, entries at 500 and 5000). Level: unit.

C3 — criterion: marks are drawn on their own lane's row. `timelineHtml([main with one 'llm_request' mark at 100, agent:agt-a with two 'tool' marks at 400 and 600], window)`: `laneRow(html,'main')` contains exactly one `data-activity-kind="llm_request"` and no `data-activity-kind="tool"`; `laneRow(html,'agent:agt-a')` contains exactly two `data-activity-kind="tool"`; each mark's style is `left:NN.NNN%` matching `activityMarks` for that lane. Level: unit.

C4 — criterion: activity that resolves to no agent instance stays visible. A three-lane payload whose unattributed lane carries one mark: `laneRow(html,'unattributed')` contains that mark, and the main row contains none. Level: unit.

C5 — criterion: the curve's geometry. `contextAreaPoints(lane with context [{atMs:0,length:100},{atMs:500,length:200},{atMs:1000,length:400}], {startMs:0,endMs:1000}, 400)` equals exactly `'0.000,100.000 0.000,75.000 50.000,50.000 100.000,0.000 100.000,100.000'`. Level: unit.

C6 — edge, empty: `contextAreaPoints` returns `''` for a lane with an empty context, and `''` when peak is 0 even though samples exist. Level: unit.

C7 — edge, single sample: a lane whose only sample is at atMs 500 with length equal to the peak yields `'50.000,100.000 50.000,0.000 50.400,0.000 50.400,100.000'` — the MIN_AREA_WIDTH_PCT rule keeps an instant curve visible. Level: unit.

C8 — criterion: growth is readable, and lanes are comparable. Two lanes with contextPeak 100 and 400: `contextPeakOf(items)` is 400, and in `timelineHtml` the 400-lane's polygon reaches y 0.000 while the 100-lane's smallest y is 75.000 (a lane consuming a quarter as much draws a quarter as high). Level: unit.

C9 — criterion: the curve is drawn behind the activity, in the rendered markup. In `timelineHtml`, a lane with samples has, inside its row, `class="lane-context"` before `class="lane-bar"` before the first `class="activity-mark"`, and its `<polygon points="…">` is non-empty; a lane with no samples has no `lane-context` element in its row. Level: unit.

C10 — criterion: the view names the measure. With at least one lane carrying context, `timelineHtml` output matches `/request body length/i` and `/characters/i`; with every lane's contextPeak 0, the output still matches `/request bod/i` and contains no `<polygon`. Level: unit.

C11 — criterion: per-lane growth is readable as a number. A lane with contextPeak 90000 and activityTotal 12 renders `fmtNum` forms of both in its row (`90.0k` and `12`). Level: unit.

C12 — regression, old shape: `timelineHtml([lane without activity/activityTotal/context/contextPeak], window)` renders the row with no `activity-mark`, no `lane-context`, and no `NaN` anywhere in the output. Level: unit.

C13 — escaping: a mark whose `name` is `'<script>x</script>'` produces no `<script` in the output (mirrors the existing hostile-agentType case). Level: unit.

Deliberately untested here: colours, pixel heights and any CSS — nothing in styles.css is asserted anywhere in this project, and pinning it would fail on every visual improvement.

===== D. tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs =====
Framework node:test with the file's own fake DOM: `installFakes(routes)` stubs document/window/location/EventSource/setInterval/fetch, `bootApp(routes, predicate)` imports a fresh `../public/app.js?case=N` and settles, `handle.el('detail').innerHTML` is the rendered session view, `handle.fire(id, type, event)` dispatches, `clickOn(sel, match)` builds a click. Routes are the `baseRoutes` object; the lane payloads are `agentsOne` (sess-1: main, two researcher instances, one unattributed) and `agentsTwo`. This file is the only place that proves the drawn result reaches the page. Run just this file: `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs`.

Preparation: extend the `agentsOne` fixture lanes with the new fields — main: `activity` [{atMs: T0+500, kind:'llm_request', name:'claude-opus-5'}, {atMs: T0+3000, kind:'tool', name:'Read'}], `activityTotal` 2, `context` [{atMs: T0+500, length: 20000}, {atMs: T0+8000, length: 90000}], `contextPeak` 90000; agent:agt-a: one 'tool' mark at T0+1500 and one sample of 30000, contextPeak 30000; agent:agt-b: empty arrays, contextPeak 0; unattributed: one 'tool' mark at T0+6500 named 'Bash' and one sample of 5000, contextPeak 5000. Leave `agentsTwo` without the new fields — it then doubles as the old-shape case in the existing switch-session test.

D1 — criterion (what proves the increment): booting the app on sess-1 renders, inside `detail`, the main lane row with a `data-activity-kind="llm_request"` and a `data-activity-kind="tool"` mark and a `<polygon points="…"` with a non-empty points list; the agt-b row has no polygon; the four `data-lane-id=` rows are still there and no technical view is selected. Use the same row-splitting approach as C (a local helper or an inline split on `data-lane-id="`). Level: end-to-end against the fake DOM.

D2 — criterion: unattributed activity reaches the page, and the page names the measure. The unattributed row contains its activity mark, and `detail.innerHTML` matches `/request body length/i`. Level: end-to-end against the fake DOM.

Deliberately untested here: that switching sessions redraws marks (D1 plus the existing switch-session case already cover both halves), and anything about the demo emitter — `tools/argus/scripts/` has no test file in this repository and this increment adds none.

return.summary: Each timeline lane now carries activity marks and a context curve: the collector joins tool/llm_request spans and api_request_body records onto the existing lane keys, and the timeline view draws them as ticks over a session-scaled SVG area with a legend naming the measure.
deviations: The plan says the context pass should 'call contentOf(log) and skip a null', but three planned tests (A5, A6, A9) feed api_request_body records that carry only body_length with no body and no body_ref, for which contentOf returns null; I added a small store-level helper requestBodyLength(log) that uses contentOf(log).length when contentOf returns content and otherwise the reported attrs.body_length, skipping the record only when neither exists, so the reported untruncated length still wins in every case and those tests pass without editing them.

The plan leaves the mark's title and the legend's exact sentence to the implementer; the title is 'tool call: <name>' / 'API request: <name>' (kind alone when the name is null) and the legend is the plan's example wording, which satisfies the phrases the tests require.

The demo emitter's growth formula is mine: main-lane body_length is max(500, 18000 + sequence*9000 + llmCallIndex*6300 +/- jitter) and each subagent's is max(500, 6000 + sequence*3000 + i*2500 +/- jitter); a local smoke run produced a monotonically rising main curve (27404 -> 60032 over 8 samples) with eight subagent lanes each carrying one sample.

increments.title: Scrubbing the timeline, and a live mode that follows the head
increments.goal: Give the timeline a chosen time that can be moved to any point of the recorded session, plus a live mode that follows the newest data as it arrives.
criteria: The timeline can be scrubbed backward and forward to any point of the recorded session, and the chosen time is visible on the timeline.
A live mode follows the newest data as it arrives.
Scrubbing away from the head leaves live mode.
A control returns to live mode.
The chosen time is one shared value the session view works from, so a later per-lane detail can be answered for exactly that moment.

What proves this increment is the behaviour of the page: a change that stops scrubbing moving the chosen time, or stops the live control returning to the head, is caught, not only a helper that maps a position to a time.
increments.note: Re-cut after timeline-landing. Two criteria added, none removed. The chosen time is named as one shared value because context-at-time, which follows, has to answer for exactly that moment, and timeline-landing showed the session view already keeps its timeline window in one place. The provability criterion carries forward the lesson that cost timeline-landing both correction rounds: a pinned pure helper is not a pinned behaviour.

increments.title: The selected agent's context and tool use as of the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, that agent's or the main session's context at that moment as a structured, expandable message list, together with the tools that agent has used up to that moment.
criteria: Selecting a lane at the chosen time shows that agent's - or the main session's - context as of that moment.

The lane selected is one of the lanes the timeline already draws, and the records shown are chosen by that lane and the chosen time using the lane vocabulary already in place, not a second attribution scheme.
The context shown is the body of the nearest API request at or before the chosen time.
It is rendered as a structured message list distinguishing system prompt, user, assistant, tool call and tool result blocks.
Each block is collapsed to one line carrying its size.
Each block expands to the exact full text the record carries, and a body the CLI truncated is marked as truncated instead of being presented as the whole context.
The same selection also shows the tools that agent has used up to that moment, each entry carrying the tool name and that call's parameters.
Both listings are per agent and per time, so 'which tools, and what for' is answerable for any agent at any point of the session.

What proves this increment is the rendered panel: a change that stops a selection reaching the panel, or stops an expanded block showing the full text, is caught, not only a builder function checked in isolation.
increments.note: Re-cut after timeline-landing. Kept whole - it still absorbs the dropped tools-at-time - with two criteria added: the selection reuses the lane vocabulary the collector serves ('main', 'agent:<agent_id>', 'unattributed') rather than a second join, and the panel is proved where it is seen. Both come from timeline-landing: it placed the join collector-side and it lost two correction rounds to behaviour that lived only in untested page wiring.

increments.title: The selected agent's tool use up to the chosen time
increments.goal: Show, for the lane selected at the chosen time, the tools that agent has used up to that moment together with the parameters of each call.
increments.note: Merged into context-at-time, which now carries all three of its criteria. content-pipeline showed tool parameters arrive as the same content records as request bodies, retrieved through the same query with the same time bound and the same per-agent join, so building them as a separate increment would repeat that increment's selection and attribution work for the sake of one extra list in the same panel.

return.summary: Closed timeline-landing as done (review accepted, no findings, after two correction rounds that were both test gaps rather than defects) and re-cut the three open increments against what it showed. Nothing was split, merged, dropped or reordered: the run confirmed the cut rather than contradicting it. Two facts changed the criteria. First, timeline-landing placed the record-to-agent join collector-side and fixed a lane vocabulary - every span of a session resolves to 'main', 'agent:<agent_id>' or 'unattributed', by agent_id first and the parent-span chain second, served by GET /api/sessions/:id/agents - so lane-activity and context-at-time now carry a criterion each that they select records by that same vocabulary instead of building a second attribution scheme, and lane-activity carries the unattributed-stays-visible criterion explicitly. Content-pipeline had already shown that body events carry no agent_id, which makes the span chain the only route from a content record to a lane; lane-activity's researcher settles that route first, since it is the last load-bearing unknown of the issue. Second, both of timeline-landing's correction rounds went on behaviour that was computed by a well-tested pure helper and never pinned in the rendered page - first the lane geometry, then the landing wiring itself - so each of the three open increments now carries one criterion demanding that what the human sees is what proves it done. The fake-DOM harness that round 2 built (tools/argus-ui/test/app.test.mjs boots public/app.js in-process) makes that cheap now, which is why the criterion is affordable. Order unchanged and deliberate: lane-activity first because per-lane attribution of activity and size records is the riskiest remaining piece, scrub-live second because it establishes the one chosen time, context-at-time last because it answers for exactly that time on exactly those lanes.
